summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, COPD, insulin-dependent diabetes, and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for acute decompensated systolic heart failure, likely triggered by high-sodium food intake and excessive fluid consumption. He presented with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and weight gain. Treatment included IV diuresis with furosemide, transitioned to oral torsemide 200 mg daily, resulting in improved symptoms and weight reduction to 83 kg. His kidney function improved from a creatinine of 2.3 to 1.8, and hyponatremia resolved with fluid restriction. A gout flare was managed with a short course of prednisone, requiring temporary insulin dose adjustment. He was discharged home with a visiting nurse, instructions to monitor daily weights, limit fluid and salt intake, avoid cocaine and tobacco, and follow up with outpatient care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
